cap_config_read.label: Configuration read
cap_config_read.description: Read Home Assistant configuration and event listener counts.

cap_camera_read.label: Camera image read
cap_camera_read.description: Retrieve still images from explicitly permitted Home Assistant cameras.

cap_template_render.label: Template render
cap_template_render.description: Render Jinja templates using entities this access key can access.

cap_log_read.label: System log read
cap_log_read.description: Read Home Assistant system log entries.

cap_log_control.label: Integration log levels
cap_log_control.description: Inspect and change process-wide log levels for accessible integrations. Verbose logging may use disk space and expose sensitive third-party output.

cap_search.label: Search & discovery
cap_search.description: Find and describe entities, areas, and relationships within this access key's scope.

cap_registry_read.label: Registry read
cap_registry_read.description: List areas, floors, zones, and devices that contain accessible entities.

cap_traces.label: Automation traces
cap_traces.description: Read execution traces to troubleshoot automations.

cap_diagnostics.label: Diagnostics
cap_diagnostics.description: Check system health and validate automation, script, and scene YAML.

cap_broadcast.label: Broadcast
cap_broadcast.description: Make announcements through Assist satellite devices.

cap_service_response.label: Service response data
cap_service_response.description: Return data from services that provide a response, such as conversation.process.

cap_automation_write.label: Manage automations
cap_automation_write.description: Create, edit, and delete automations. Bypasses entity-level access controls.

cap_script_write.label: Manage scripts
cap_script_write.description: Create, edit, and delete scripts. Bypasses entity-level access controls.

cap_blueprint_write.label: Manage blueprints
cap_blueprint_write.description: Create, edit, and delete blueprints. Also requires the matching automation or script capability. Editing a blueprint reloads every automation or script built from it, so one change can rewire several at once.

cap_scene_write.label: Manage scenes
cap_scene_write.description: Create, edit, and delete scenes. Referenced entities are still subject to MESA and entity access.

cap_helper_write.label: Manage helpers
cap_helper_write.description: Create, edit, and delete helpers such as inputs, counters, and timers.

cap_physical_control.label: Physical control
cap_physical_control.description: Control locks, alarms, covers, and valves.

cap_restart.label: Restart or stop Home Assistant
cap_restart.description: Allow homeassistant.restart and homeassistant.stop service calls.

cap_integration_write.label: Integration management
cap_integration_write.description: List, update, reload, enable, disable, and remove accessible Home Assistant integrations.

cap_integration_reconfigure.label: Integration reconfiguration
cap_integration_reconfigure.description: Submit reviewed credentials, hosts, and other values through Home Assistant's official reconfigure flow. Phoenix cannot automatically roll changes back.

cap_lovelace_write.label: Manage dashboards
cap_lovelace_write.description: Create, edit, and delete Lovelace dashboards.

cap_registry_write.label: Manage entity registry
cap_registry_write.description: Edit entity names, icons, and areas, or delete stale entries. Entity IDs cannot be renamed.

cap_radio_write.label: Radio management
cap_radio_write.description: Scan topology and manage Zigbee devices through Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA.

cap_energy_write.label: Manage Energy dashboard
cap_energy_write.description: Change which statistics feed the Energy dashboard: grid, solar, battery, gas, water, and individual devices.

cap_backup.label: Backup
cap_backup.description: Create and list backups. Restore them from Home Assistant.

cap_filesystem.label: Read files
cap_filesystem.description: Read files under www/, themes/, and custom_templates/.

cap_dashboard_resources.label: Dashboard resources
cap_dashboard_resources.description: List, add, change and remove the JavaScript and CSS files every dashboard loads, which is how custom cards are installed. A registered JavaScript file runs in every browser that opens a dashboard, with that person's Home Assistant access, so Confirm is strongly recommended.

cap_esphome_yaml.label: ESPHome device YAML
cap_esphome_yaml.description: Read ESPHome device YAML in its own jail under esphome/, validate it, and compile it. Credentials are masked on read. Compiling only builds a binary; flashing a device needs the separate ESPHome firmware flashing capability.

cap_esphome_flash.label: ESPHome firmware flashing
cap_esphome_flash.description: Install compiled firmware onto an ESPHome device over the air, replacing what it is running. A bad image can leave a device unreachable until it is reflashed over a cable, so Confirm is strongly recommended.

cap_yaml_edit.label: YAML configuration
cap_yaml_edit.description: Read configuration.yaml and the other YAML files in the configuration directory, check the configuration, and reload domains defined in YAML. Inline secrets are exposed, so store secrets in secrets.yaml with !secret.

caps.modeDescConfirm: Queue each call for approval in this panel.
caps.passThroughNotice: Pass-through is enabled. Reads and everyday actions are treated as Allow. Configuration changes, system actions, high-risk capabilities, system log access, and camera image reads still use the settings below. Confirm always requires approval.
caps.esphomeBadgeTitle: The ESPHome tools stay hidden from this access key until the add-on is available. The capability can still be set now.

cap_calendar_write.label: Calendar write
cap_calendar_write.description: Create, update and delete events on writable calendars.

automation_builder.label: Automation builder
automation_builder.description: Can discover entities and manage automations, scripts, scenes, and helpers. Restarts and physical controls require approval.

dashboard_designer.label: Dashboard designer
dashboard_designer.description: Can discover entities, build dashboards, and read theme and custom card files. Registering custom card files requires approval. Cannot control devices or edit other configuration.

esphome.label: ESPHome devices
esphome.description: Reads ESPHome device status, diagnostics, logs, and device YAML, and validates and compiles it. Flashing firmware needs approval. YAML credentials stay hidden. No device control or other configuration.

personas.helper: A persona sets the initial capabilities. You can adjust individual capabilities in Advanced. The persona changes to Custom when your settings no longer match a preset.

home_admin.label: Home administrator
home_admin.description: Can read and manage the whole home. Restarts, physical controls, and sensitive configuration changes require approval.

maintenance.label: Maintenance / backups
maintenance.description: Can run diagnostics and create backups. Restarts and entity registry changes require approval. Cannot control devices or edit configuration and dashboards.

new_user.label: New user
new_user.description: Can read your home and control only the devices you grant. Locks, alarms, covers, and valves require approval. You can change this later.

personas.noEsphome: ESPHome was not detected on this system

power_user.label: Power user
power_user.description: Can read and edit most configuration and restart Home Assistant. Sensitive system changes require approval. File and YAML configuration access stay blocked.

read_only.label: Read-only observer
read_only.description: Can read states, history, logs, and templates. Cannot run actions or announcements.

voice_assistant.label: Voice assistant
voice_assistant.description: Can read entities, run services, and make announcements. Locks, alarms, covers, and valves require approval.

home_companion.label: Home Companion
home_companion.description: Designed for Agent Chat and Voice: one task tool for household reads and device control. Uses the Voice conversation model.
home_companion.setup: Choose a provider and model in Voice settings. Grant READ or WRITE through the normal permission tree. Capabilities enable or disable access within the household catalog; configuration and authoring tools stay unavailable. Pass-through and announce-all are disabled.

wizard.accessSub: Expand the light group and choose a light you can verify. Select W to grant read and write access. Grant a whole device or expand it to choose one entity. You can add more permissions later.
wizard.agentClaudeHint: Run in the project directory, then check with claude mcp list. For all projects, add --scope user.
wizard.agentCodexIntro: Use the CLI command, app settings, or configuration file below. Choose one setup method.
wizard.agentCursorIntro: Add this to ~/.cursor/mcp.json for all projects, or .cursor/mcp.json for one project. Then enable the server under Cursor Settings > MCP.
wizard.agentGeminiHint: Run in the project directory, then check with gemini mcp list. For all projects, add --scope user.
wizard.agentOtherIntro: Example for clients accepting mcpServers JSON with HTTP transport and custom headers. Follow your client's configuration format.
wizard.chatReadySub: You can test your agent now using the Agent Chat window. A test question is already typed in for you; press Send. This wizard closes once you send your first prompt.
wizard.choiceAppBody: Use Claude Code, an IDE, or another MCP app that accepts a bearer access key. Copy the generated connection command or configuration.
wizard.choiceChatBody: Chat in a window right here in Home Assistant. Bring an API key from a model provider, or a local Ollama server. Nothing to install.
wizard.chooseSub: You can chat with your agent entirely within Home Assistant using the API key or local hostname of your model provider. Optionally, you can use an external app to connect to Phoenix MCP. Select your preferred option:
wizard.codexAppSettingsHint: In the app's MCP server settings, add a Streamable HTTP server named {serverName} with the URL above. Use the Authorization header below and leave the bearer-token environment field empty. Save and reconnect.
wizard.codexConfigFileHint: Alternative: add this table to ~/.codex/config.toml or this project's .codex/config.toml. Set the access key environment variable before starting Codex.
wizard.codexEnvHint: macOS/Linux: run this in the shell that starts Codex; add the export to your shell profile for future sessions. PowerShell: set $env:{envVar}="phx_..."; setx only affects new processes. Separately launched apps may not inherit shell variables, so use the app header fields.
wizard.connectAgentTitle: Connect Phoenix MCP to your AI agent
wizard.connectIntro: Add Phoenix MCP as an MCP server in your agent. It authenticates with Authorization: Bearer phx_..., not Home Assistant login or OAuth. Use HTTPS across untrusted networks. Keep bearer access keys out of shell history, shared files, screenshots and version control. Rotate an access key if disclosed.
wizard.connected: Connected! Your agent reached Phoenix MCP.
wizard.createFailed: Failed to create the access key.
wizard.doneSub: Access key {name} is ready. You can change its capabilities and permissions from the access key page. Revoke it when it is no longer needed, then delete it from Archived access keys.
wizard.mesaHint: MESA may require approval for control actions. The read prompt is enough to verify the connection.
wizard.nameError: Name must be 3-32 characters: letters, digits, _ or -.
wizard.noLights: No lights found in this Home Assistant.
wizard.personaSub: Create a scoped test access key, grant access to one device, and connect your agent. New user is selected as a cautious starting point. Choose another persona if needed.
wizard.promptChat: How many lights are in my home?
wizard.providerAddFirst: Add a provider account to continue.
wizard.providerIntro: Agent Chat runs your agent inside Home Assistant using your own model provider account.
wizard.providerPickExisting: Pick an account you already added, or add a new one.
wizard.serverNameHint: Each access key uses a separate server name. Enable only one Phoenix MCP server at a time to avoid duplicate tools with different permissions.
wizard.skillClaudeHint: Install the Phoenix MCP guide as a Claude Code skill. Run this in your terminal.
wizard.skillCodexHint: Install the guide at ~/.agents/skills/phoenix/SKILL.md. Restart Codex if it is not listed under /skills.
wizard.skillCursorHint: Run from the project root. The .mdc rule loads the downloaded guide when Phoenix MCP is relevant.
wizard.skillGeminiHint: Install the guide at ~/.gemini/skills/phoenix/SKILL.md, then run /skills reload in Gemini.
wizard.skillInstallTitle: Optional: install the Phoenix MCP skill
wizard.skillOtherHint: Download the guide and add it to your agent's project context or rules. The agent can also fetch it from the URL below.
wizard.skillSectionBody: Install the Phoenix MCP skill to explain scoped permissions, approvals, and MESA rules to {label}. Phoenix MCP also shares this guidance when the agent connects.
wizard.testSub: Send this prompt to your agent. Phoenix MCP will detect the connection.
wizard.accessKeyCreatedBanner: Access key created. You can rename it later; cancel and start over to change its expiry.
wizard.accessKeySub: Use a dedicated access key for testing. You can change the suggested name now, and rename it later from the access key's page. The expiry cannot be changed after creation.
wizard.urlHint: If the agent runs on another machine or network, use a Home Assistant URL it can reach, such as your Nabu Casa or external HTTPS URL.
wizard.waitingForAgent: Waiting for your agent to connect...
wizard.agentHarnessIntro: Use the desktop app or CLI. Configure your model account in Harness. Phoenix support is experimental during Harness's preview; this client is separate from Agent Chat's DeepSeek API provider.
wizard.harnessConfigHint: Open Harness once, then fully quit it. If this file is missing, create it; otherwise append this - insert: block as another top-level list item. Preserve existing content and keep your access key private. Save, then reopen Harness. With custom DSH_HOME, use its profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml.
wizard.harnessLaunchHint: CLI only: save the same YAML as a new phoenix.cordis.yml file in your working directory, install Node.js, then run this command. It starts the web interface, not the desktop app.
wizard.skillHarnessHint: Install the guide at ~/.dsh/skills/phoenix/SKILL.md. With a custom DSH_HOME, use its skills directory instead.

If the model has not said whether it accepts images, Phoenix also sends one small test image and reads the answer. This uses your own API credit. settings.agentcliGlobalAria: Show Agent Chat throughout Home Assistant

settings.agentcliIntro: Chat with Home Assistant using your own model provider. Agent Chat follows the selected access key's permissions, approvals, and MESA rules. Add a provider account, then open Agent Chat from the top right corner.
settings.agentcliRemoveBody: Remove {name}? Agent Chat will no longer be able to use this account until you add it again.
settings.agentcliScrollbackHelp: Lines kept for display and conversation context. Use 0 for no history. Recommended: 100 to 500. Maximum: 5,000.
settings.agentcliStepsHelp: Tool rounds the agent runs before pausing to ask whether to continue. Higher means fewer interruptions on deep tasks. Range: 3 to 100.
settings.agentcliValidated: Connection validated. Choose a model to continue.
settings.aiTaskBehaviorFreeTextOnly: These choices apply only to free-text output. Structured tasks follow their schema without style or detail instructions.

settings.aiTaskDefaultModalBody: Data generation actions that do not specify an entity will use Phoenix MCP AI Task.
settings.aiTaskDefaultModalNotReady: Select an access key, provider account, and model first. Then return here to make Phoenix MCP the default.
settings.aiTaskDefaultModalReplaces: Home Assistant allows only one default, so this replaces the current one: {name}.
settings.aiTaskDefaultModalTitle: Make Phoenix MCP the default AI Task?
settings.aiTaskDefaultOff: Use Phoenix MCP when a Data generation action does not specify an entity.
settings.aiTaskDefaultOn: Phoenix MCP handles Data generation actions that do not specify an entity.
settings.aiTaskDisableBody: Phoenix MCP AI Task is the current default for Data generation tasks. Disabling it also clears that default. Home Assistant will use another entity if one is available.
settings.aiTaskDisableTitle: Disable the Phoenix MCP AI Task?
settings.aiTaskEnableHelp: Add Phoenix MCP AI Task as an entity that automations, scripts, and dashboards can use. Use the setup below (recommended), or go to HA > Settings > Voice assistants
settings.aiTaskIntro: Run Home Assistant AI Task actions through Phoenix MCP's model with access key permissions, approvals, MESA rules, and audit logging.
settings.aiTaskModelHelp: The model used for this AI Task.
settings.aiTaskProviderHelp: The provider account used to run this AI Task.
settings.aiTaskSetDefaultFailed: Could not set the default AI Task entity.
settings.aiTaskAccessKeyHelp: Controls which entities and actions this AI Task can access.
settings.aiTaskUnsupported: AI Task is unavailable in this Home Assistant installation. Check the Home Assistant logs, then reload Phoenix MCP.
settings.assistBoundHelp: Only one access key can be bound. In your LLM integration, set Control Home Assistant to Phoenix MCP (scoped). Then select that agent under HA > Settings > Voice assistants, turn off Prefer handling commands locally, and make it preferred.
settings.detailBalancedHelp: Enough context to understand and act, normally as a short paragraph or compact list.
settings.detailConciseHelp: A few sentences or minimal steps with essential caveats.
settings.detailDetailedHelp: Thorough reasoning, steps, tradeoffs, and caveats without repetition.
settings.homeFocusedHelp: Focus preference, not a security control. Requests not directly about your Home Assistant installation are declined, and there is no override.
settings.assistIntro: Give an existing Home Assistant LLM integration access to Phoenix MCP's scoped tools. Choose Phoenix MCP (scoped) when configuring that agent. Use Voice Agent (above) if you want Phoenix MCP to manage the model.
settings.assistUnsupported: This feature is not supported by your Home Assistant version.
settings.dataBody: Permanently delete selected Phoenix MCP data. Core Phoenix MCP data, Agent Chat provider keys, and MESA profiles can be deleted separately.
settings.flushIntervalHelp: Never disables periodic audit saves. Home Assistant stop, reload and unload still attempt a final save.
settings.infoStorageNote: Phoenix MCP configuration is stored in .storage/phoenix_mcp.json and is included in all HA full backups and partial backups of the .storage directory.
settings.injectHelp: Add MESA profile buttons to Home Assistant's Automations, Scripts, Helpers, People, and integration pages. These buttons may need a Phoenix MCP update after a Home Assistant frontend change. Reload Home Assistant after changing this. Admins only.
settings.injectUnavailable: Temporarily disabled because this Home Assistant version is not compatible with the profile buttons. A future Phoenix MCP update may restore this feature.
settings.killSwitchActiveAria: Kill switch active. All Phoenix MCP endpoints are disabled
settings.killSwitchActiveHelp: All Phoenix MCP client requests are now refused. Re-enabling will re-register all Phoenix MCP routes immediately, without an HA restart.
settings.killSwitchActiveLabel: Kill switch ACTIVE - All Phoenix MCP endpoints are disabled
settings.killSwitchInactiveHelp: When enabled, MCP, context, skill, Agent Chat, Voice Agent and AI Task refuse new work. Assist exposes zero tools. The admin panel remains accessible.
settings.languageHelp: Panel language. Auto follows your Home Assistant profile.
settings.logAllowedHelp: Record successful requests in the audit log.
settings.logClientIpHelp: Show source IP addresses. When off, they appear as [redacted].
settings.logDeniedHelp: Record denied and not-found requests in the audit log.
settings.logDisableAllHelp: Stops new audit entries. Sensor counters continue to update.
settings.logEntityIdsHelp: Show entity IDs in the resource field. When off, they appear as [redacted].
settings.logRateLimitedHelp: Record requests blocked by a rate limit.
settings.maxLogEntriesHelp: Maximum entries kept in memory and on disk. Lowering this removes the oldest entries immediately.
settings.mesaEnforcedWarning: Entities without a MESA profile use the built-in safety baseline. Locks and alarm panels are blocked; most other domains require approval. Add profiles or deployment defaults before relying on Enforced mode.
settings.mesaModeHelp: Advisory warns about most policy limits; read-only and explicit privacy denials still block. Enforced blocks prohibited actions and queues confirmation requests.
settings.notifyApprovalHelp: Send a Home Assistant notification for new approval requests. The Approvals count always updates.
settings.notifyRateLimitHelp: Send a Home Assistant notification when an access key reaches its rate limit, at most once per access key each minute.
settings.notifyRateLimitLabel: Notify when a rate limit is reached
settings.presetsHelp: Lets you save several named setups for each access key and switch between them, for example a locked-down everyday setup and a broader one for maintenance. A preset stores the key's capabilities, permissions, rate limits, and pass-through setting. When you turn this on, each access key starts with one preset made from its current settings. When you switch presets, any unsaved changes are saved into the preset you're leaving first.
settings.styleCalmGuideHelp: Patient, reassuring, accessible, and never patronizing.
settings.styleDirectHelp: Plain, efficient, matter-of-fact, and outcome first.
settings.styleLivelyHelp: Energetic, with occasional light humor only when stakes are low.
settings.styleTechnicalHelp: Precise terminology with compact implementation detail.
settings.styleWarmHelp: Friendly and encouraging without praise, flattery, or padding.
settings.themeHelp: Light, dark, or follow system preference.

settings.voiceAssistSetupNone: Create and configure a Home Assistant assistant for this voice agent.
settings.voiceConfigureFirst: Select an access key, provider, and model first.

settings.voiceDisableTitle: Disable the Phoenix MCP voice agent?
settings.voiceEnableHelp: Add Phoenix MCP as a conversation agent. Use the setup below (recommended), or select Phoenix MCP under HA > Settings > Voice assistants, turn off "Prefer handling commands locally," and make it preferred.

settings.voiceModelHelp: The model used for this voice agent.
settings.voicePreferredHelp: Use Phoenix MCP by default. You can change this under Settings > Voice assistants.
settings.voicePreferredLabel: Make Phoenix MCP my preferred assistant
settings.voiceProviderHelp: The provider account used to run this voice agent.

settings.voiceSetupTitle: Set up the Phoenix MCP voice assistant
settings.voiceAccessKeyHelp: Controls which entities and actions this voice agent can access.
